subject: Design guidance: internal cert broker + VPC ingress / TLS termination for private endpoints
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@finsight.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@finsight.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Private endpoints: cert + DNS model for our VPC deployment

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward Redwood Private (VPC) and our security/compliance team has a few hard requirements around TLS termination and certificate provenance for internal endpoints:

- All customer-facing control-plane endpoints must be TLS with certs rooted in our corporate PKI (we cannot use public CAs for internal endpoints).
- We need automated rotation without manual handoffs.
- Split-horizon DNS is acceptable but must be auditable.

Can you recommend architecture patterns and what Redwood can manage vs what must remain customer-owned? We're targeting an on-prem + VPC hybrid and would like a short ops checklist.

Best,
Alice
---
Alice Gomez
Head of Platform Security, FinSight PBC
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@finsight.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints: cert + DNS model for our VPC deployment

Alice — thanks, and great questions. High level answer first, then a recommended ops model and checklist attached. Short summary:

1) Termination location choices (trade-offs)
  - Customer-edge TLS termination (recommended for strict PKI control): TLS terminated at the customer's LB / edge proxy with certs issued by their corporate CA. Redwood instances see plaintext behind the customer-controlled network or can use mTLS downstream. Pros: full control, auditable CA. Cons: increased complexity for health probes and can complicate mutual auth.
  - Terminate at Redwood ingress (Envoy/HAProxy) inside the VPC (Redwood-managed): we can accept certs you provide (private CA chain) and handle rotation on your schedule via a broker integration. Pros: simpler for customer apps; Cons: requires you to share certs or allow a certificate signing flow.
  - TLS passthrough to backend (SNI routing): best for workloads where Redwood must not terminate TLS (e.g., PCI). Requires TCP-level routing (NLB) and SNI-based routing.

2) Certificate provisioning patterns
  - Customer CA + ACME-like internal CA: run an internal ACME server (e.g., smallstep/step-ca) or cert-manager tied to your PKI/HSM. Redwood can integrate to fetch certs via a secure API.
  - PKI-only: you push signed cert bundles to a Redwood certificate broker endpoint (audit logs recorded).
  - Vault-based issuance: HashiCorp Vault PKI role that Redwood can call with short-lived cert issuance (recommended when you want rotation without handing out intermediate/private keys).

3) DNS model (split-horizon)
  - Use private hosted zones (Route53, Cloud DNS) or on-prem DNS. Public DNS stays unchanged; internal names resolve to private IPs or load balancer endpoints. Redwood supports registering the private hostname and verifying ownership via an out-of-band token.

4) Automation & rotation
  - Short-lived certs (7–30 days) rotated automatically via broker or vault.
  - Audit trail: every issuance/rotation logged to the customer's audit sink and Redwood's console.

I've attached a short ops checklist and a concise design doc (internal-cert-brokering-design.pdf). Next steps I propose:
  - Quick call to confirm whether you prefer customer-edge termination or brokered Redwood-managed termination.
  - If customer-edge: we'll provide ALB/NLB health probe guidance and a minimal mTLS handshake spec.
  - If brokered: we'll exchange an API key and a CSR flow; Redwood will accept the intermediate cert signed by your CA.

Looping Karthik (networking) and Neha (security/compliance) to validate details.

Thanks,
Rishi

Adding a few network-specific constraints we should surface to FinSight:

- If customer terminates TLS at edge: ensure health checks terminate properly. Recommend TCP health checks + a shared secret header for app probes. For HTTPS health checks with edge certs, we need a cert chain that includes the probe CA or disable strict verification for the probes.
- For split-horizon DNS: avoid CNAME chains that point to external hostnames. Prefer A/AAAA records in the private zone or alias records to a private NLB.
- SNI routing: we will support SNI-based routing on our NLBs only when the SNI value maps to a pre-registered hostname in our control plane. Make sure the upstream proxy preserves the original SNI for passthrough cases.
- MTLS: recommend customer uses mTLS between their edge and Redwood control-plane with client certs issued by their PKI. For simplicity, we can require a single CA bundle for client cert verification per account.

I'll put these into the checklist spreadsheet as concrete config snippets (NLB vs ALB differences, headers, ports).

-karthik
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Alice — for compliance, a few non-negotiables from our side if you choose Redwood-managed broker flow:

- Private key ownership: we do NOT retain customer private keys. If you want Redwood to perform CSR + sign via your CA, we only accept an intermediate signed by your PKI (we keep only the intermediate cert and never the root private key).
- HSM/KMS: integrate issuance calls with your HSM (PKCS#11) or Vault; Redwood will call a short-lived issuance endpoint and will not persist private keys.
- Auditability: every cert request and rotation event will be emitted to your audit log endpoint (HTTPS webhook) and to our console.
- Revocation: you must provide OCSP/CRL endpoints if you require runtime revocation checks. We recommend short-lived certs over revocation where possible.

If you remain required to keep certificates on-prem (no intermediates allowed off-prem), then the customer-edge termination option is the path forward and we'll focus on mTLS + probe accommodations.

I'll schedule a follow-up call to walk through the checklist; rishi, can you propose times?

—Neha
